Subject: Next steps + procurement questions — Redwood pricing & packaging

Hi Priya / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Agreed POC scope: integration of Redwood Hosted API for ingestion + low-latency generation for the analytics UI (approx 2–5s latency target).
- Production target: Q3 (scale after successful POC).
- Key procurement constraints: your team needs PO-based billing for vendor payments; smaller purchases on card are possible under $10k.

Open questions we want to confirm to align pricing/packaging: 
1) Procurement path: do you want Redwood to bill via PO (standard contract) or pursue AWS Marketplace listing / procurement? If PO, please confirm contact and preferred contract flow (SOW + PO, or Master Services Agreement + PO).
2) Payment method rules: you mentioned card ok for <$10k — is that per invoice or per month?
3) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: for POC we typically recommend Hosted on on-demand (no commit) and then evaluate Dedicated reserved capacity when you have predictable QPS/tokens. Is your procurement team okay starting with an on-demand Hosted contract and committing later?
4) Committed vs on-demand economics: to size any Dedicated commit we need a rough monthly usage estimate (tokens/day or average QPS).

Attachments: redwood-pricing-20260305.pdf (summary pricing + commit tiers), draft_sow_marissa_20260305.docx (PO-friendly SOW template).

Next steps: 
- Priya/Tom: confirm procurement contact + whether Marketplace is preferred, and answer Q2–Q4 above.
- We (Neha + Marissa): can put together a short one-page table that maps expected usage to Hosted on-demand vs Dedicated commits and estimated monthly cost.
- If useful, we can schedule a short follow-up (30 min) with our Solutions Architect to size Dedicated vs Hosted for POC.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your procurement preference and a rough usage ballpark.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- Procurement path: Our default is PO against a signed MS A or SOW. We can do Marketplace purchases (AWS Marketplace) but that requires our internal procurement team to confirm parity on pricing and may add a 2–3 week approval step. If we can get price parity or clear benefits, Marketplace is preferred for billing simplicity.
- Card vs PO: Card purchases are typically used for proof-of-concept or vendor evals under $10k total. That $10k is per vendor initiative (i.e., per month cap not set; it’s a small-scope threshold). For anything above that we need a PO.
- Timeline: Procurement can start the PO process in June if we decide to commit.

Clarifications we need from Redwood: 
1) Short explanation (1 paragraph) of the differences between Hosted (on-demand) vs Dedicated (reserved) vs Private (VPC/on-prem) — specifically from a billing/PO perspective (e.g., is Dedicated usually purchased as a monthly commit? Are there minimum contract durations?),
2) A canonical pricing table showing on-demand rates and at least two commit tiers (monthly commit + discount), and whether purchasing via AWS Marketplace changes rates or billing cadence.

I’ve attached our procurement intake form (acme_procurement_form.pdf) — it includes the legal routing and PO contact details.

If you can send the one-page pricing map and answers to 1–2 above we’ll review internally and come back with a preferred path (Marketplace vs PO).

Best,
Priya Shah

Hi Priya — quick technical & commercial clarifications from our side to help Procurement evaluate options: 

- Hosted (on-demand): Fastest to start. Billed per-token (or per-embedding) monthly. No long-term commit required; good for POC. No infra commitment means variable monthly spend.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Reserved GPU pools with a monthly commit (we typically offer 3/6/12 month commit options). Committed capacity gives a meaningful discount vs on-demand and provides predictable throughput/latency SLA. Usually purchased via PO and a committed-contract (monthly billing against the commit).

- Private (VPC / on-prem): For regulated environments. Pricing includes platform fee + support + optional infra. Usually licensed/contracted with enterprise terms and longer lead time (legal review). PO-based billing is typical.

Recommendation for Acme given today's discussion: Start POC on Hosted (on-demand) to iterate quickly. As you approach predictable steady-state (likely before Q3 production), move to a Dedicated commit (6–12 month) to capture discounts and predictable capacity.

To size Dedicated, we need a rough monthly token estimate. For context, a small Dedicated 1-card pool typically covers ~5–10M tokens/day depending on model & sequence length. Commit discounts start at ~20% for 3-month and increase for longer terms — I’ll include a one-page table.

Marissa — I’ll draft the one-page pricing map and commit-tier comparison and send by EOD today. Also happy to jump on a 30-min session with your Solutions Architect to confirm sizing if Priya wants that.

Thanks,

Thanks all — quick update from our side after internal sync: 

- Usage estimate: POC (April) roughly 200k–500k tokens/day. Production target in Q3: ~2M tokens/day (could scale up).
- Procurement timing: we can start PO paperwork in June for a Q3 production go-live. For POC we prefer to either use card (if total spend < $10k) or a short-term PO.
- Marketplace: would prefer AWS Marketplace if pricing is the same. If Marketplace adds a premium, we’ll go the PO route.

Request: Please send the one-page pricing map that Neha mentioned and a short table showing cost delta between on-demand and two commit tiers (3-month, 12-month) for our expected monthly token volumes. Also include whether Dedicated has a minimum contract or setup lead time.

Once we have that we’ll confirm whether to proceed via Marketplace or direct PO, and we can schedule the 30-min sizing call.

Thanks — Tom
